e2e.browser: Chrome headless against built Next frontend and real Nest API
scenarios: preserves password-only login, refresh cookies, and legacy version-zero access tokens
activates only after verification, encrypts the pending and active secret, hashes codes and revokes old sessions
refuses pre-2FA tokens on HTTP, WebSocket and refresh; does not record a completed login prematurely
consumes a recovery code and challenge exactly once under concurrent submissions
accepts the standard next-step tolerance but rejects expired and replayed authenticator codes
persists the five-attempt user lock across new challenges and different IP addresses
requires both the password and factor to disable, then restores password-only login and revokes sessions
restricts administrative reset to authorized users in the same organization and audits the actor and reason
invalidates a pending challenge after the password changes
rolls back factor consumption when session issuance fails, so retrying cannot lose the recovery code
rejects an expired setup and reports encrypted-secret corruption as unavailable instead of an internal error
enforces the IP limit even for invalid or forged challenge tokens
verifies setup, TOTP, recovery and disabling through the real browser UI
